intro.title: Reading: Self Introduction
intro.explanation: Read short self-introductions using vocabulary and grammar you've learned.
intro.cultureNote: In Japan, self-introductions (自己紹介) are very important in both social and business settings.

items.passage: はじめまして。私はたなかです。日本人です。学生です。よろしくお願いします。
items.translation: Nice to meet you. I am Tanaka. I am Japanese. I am a student. Please treat me well.

questions.question: What is the speaker's name?
What does the speaker do?

items.passage: 私はリンです。アメリカ人です。二十さいです。日本語の学生です。
items.translation: I am Lin. I am American. I am 20 years old. I am a Japanese language student.

questions.question: Where is Lin from?
How old is Lin?
What is Lin studying?

items.passage: こんにちは。やまだです。せんせいです。えいごのせんせいです。よろしくお願いします。
items.translation: Hello. I am Yamada. I am a teacher. I am an English teacher. Please treat me well.

questions.question: What is Yamada's job?
What subject does Yamada teach?

intro.title: Reading: My Family
intro.explanation: Read short passages about families using possessives and family vocabulary.
intro.cultureNote: Japanese uses different words for family members when talking about your own family versus someone else's family.

items.passage: 私のかぞくは四人です。父と母と姉と私です。父はかいしゃいんです。母はせんせいです。
items.translation: My family has four people. It's my father, mother, older sister, and me. My father is a company employee. My mother is a teacher.

questions.question: How many people are in the family?
What does the father do?
What does the mother do?

items.passage: 弟は十さいです。小学生です。まいにちサッカーをします。サッカーがすきです。
items.translation: My younger brother is 10 years old. He is an elementary school student. He plays soccer every day. He likes soccer.

questions.question: How old is the younger brother?
What does the brother like?

items.passage: 姉は大学生です。二十一さいです。えいごとフランスごをべんきょうします。
items.translation: My older sister is a university student. She is 21 years old. She studies English and French.

questions.question: What does the older sister study?
How old is the older sister?

intro.title: Reading: Daily Routine
intro.explanation: Read about daily routines using time expressions, verbs, and the particle に.
intro.cultureNote: Many Japanese people follow very regular daily schedules. Punctuality is highly valued in Japanese culture.

items.passage: まいあさ七じにおきます。八じにあさごはんをたべます。九じにがっこうにいきます。
items.translation: I wake up at 7 every morning. I eat breakfast at 8. I go to school at 9.

questions.question: What time does the speaker wake up?
What does the speaker do at 8 o'clock?

items.passage: 十二じにひるごはんをたべます。ともだちといっしょにたべます。おべんとうをもっていきます。
items.translation: I eat lunch at 12. I eat together with my friend. I bring a boxed lunch.

questions.question: Who does the speaker eat lunch with?
What does the speaker bring for lunch?

items.passage: よるはうちでべんきょうします。十じにおふろにはいります。十一じにねます。
items.translation: In the evening I study at home. I take a bath at 10. I go to sleep at 11.

questions.question: Where does the speaker study?
What time does the speaker go to sleep?

items.passage: にちようびはがっこうにいきません。あさはおそくおきます。テレビをみます。
items.translation: On Sunday I don't go to school. I wake up late in the morning. I watch TV.

questions.question: Does the speaker go to school on Sunday?
What does the speaker do on Sunday morning?

intro.title: Reading: At the Store
intro.explanation: Read short shopping conversations using numbers, counters, and ください.
intro.cultureNote: In Japanese stores, staff are very polite. Customers also use polite language when making requests.

items.passage: 「すみません、このりんごはいくらですか。」「一つ百円です。」「三つください。」「三百円です。」
items.translation: "Excuse me, how much is this apple?" "One is 100 yen." "Three please." "That's 300 yen."

questions.question: How much is one apple?
How many apples does the customer buy?

items.passage: デパートにいきました。くつをかいました。五千円でした。あたらしいくつはくろいです。
items.translation: I went to the department store. I bought shoes. They were 5,000 yen. The new shoes are black.

questions.question: Where did the speaker go?
What color are the new shoes?
How much were the shoes?

items.passage: スーパーでたまごとぎゅうにゅうをかいます。たまごは二百円です。ぎゅうにゅうは百五十円です。
items.translation: I buy eggs and milk at the supermarket. Eggs are 200 yen. Milk is 150 yen.

questions.question: How much are the eggs?
What does the speaker buy at the supermarket?

intro.title: Reading: Weekend Plans
intro.explanation: Read about weekend activities using past tense, future plans, and たい form.
intro.cultureNote: Japanese people often spend weekends with family or friends, visiting parks, shopping, or eating out together.

items.passage: きのうはともだちとえいがをみました。とてもおもしろかったです。そのあとでレストランでたべました。
items.translation: Yesterday I watched a movie with my friend. It was very interesting. After that we ate at a restaurant.

questions.question: What did the speaker do yesterday?
How was the movie?

items.passage: あしたはこうえんにいきたいです。天気がいいですから。おべんとうをつくりたいです。
items.translation: Tomorrow I want to go to the park. Because the weather is good. I want to make a boxed lunch.

questions.question: Where does the speaker want to go tomorrow?
Why does the speaker want to go?

items.passage: どようびにかぞくとかいものにいきました。母はふくをかいました。私はほんをかいました。たのしかったです。
items.translation: On Saturday I went shopping with my family. My mother bought clothes. I bought a book. It was fun.

questions.question: Who did the speaker go shopping with?
What did the speaker buy?
How did the speaker feel about the trip?

items.passage: 日よう日はうちにいました。あめでしたから。本をよみました。おんがくもききました。
items.translation: On Sunday I stayed at home. Because it was raining. I read a book. I also listened to music.

questions.question: Why did the speaker stay home?
What did the speaker do at home?
options: Read a book and listened to music
